notes.text: Opening argument continues with reste à voir and two cases. The prime discrepancy is transcribed, not silently repaired.
Ultra faux stands beside the corollary; condition a is globally crossed. The oblique note discusses b,c,d and a; its full reading and the uncertain cancellation state are preserved.
NB says that injectivity is what must be proved ici. No proof of that general assertion was supplied by this reader.
At the foot the author writes On va prouver p. ex, gives the four-arrow cycle, begins d=>b, and leaves the set equality as a goal with il reste à prouver.
No later scan was opened. No root decisions, other-reader outputs or crops were consulted. Reading wording, counting signs and inspecting revision strokes are not called proof checks.

checks.statement: Conditional sufficiency of the displayed set equality for the desired bijection, assuming phi fixes the common elements of F and F-prime.
checks.outcome: Passed as a conditional set-theoretic implication only.
checks.reasoning: If F-prime minus G-prime equals F minus G, and phi restricted to F minus G is the canonical inclusion into F, then its restriction with codomain F minus G is the identity on that set. The identity has itself as inverse, so the displayed map is a bijection.
checks.limits: The displayed set equality and the hypothesis that the canonical map fixes common elements were not proved here. No proof of the corollary, equivalence of b/c/d, or the asserted relation to a was performed.
